title: Top Songwriters For Morgan Wallen, Post Malone & Demi Lovato Reveal Why Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Is a Lasting Hit: ‘There Are No Wasted Notes’
summary: “Choosin’ Texas’ is now the longest non-holiday No. 1 by a solo woman artist on the Billboard Hot 100.
contentText:
Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas” is no stranger to breaking chart records, but the yearning country song recently set one of its most significant milestones yet: For the Hot 100 chart dated Aug. 1, “Choosin’ Texas” logged its 15th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, spending the most weeks ever at No. 1 for a non-holiday title by a woman with no co-billed acts.

On the current chart, Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” surpasses Whitney Houston ’s 1992 hit “I Will Always Love You” and Mariah Carey’ s 2005 smash “We Belong Together.” (Carey still has bragging rights with “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” which has spent 22 weeks in the top spot since its 1994 release.)

“Choosin’ Texas,” written by Langley, Miranda Lambert , Luke Dick and JoyBeth Taylor,  is a hummable earworm from start to finish, but what exactly makes it so catchy? Billboard asked some of the top songwriters in country and pop music, all of whom know a thing or two about writing a No. 1 hit, why “Choosin’ Texas” has struck such a chord (every pun intended) with millions of listeners. We asked them to evaluate the tune from a songwriter’s perspective; They all had different reasons on why it is has been so successful, but the one trait mentioned most was the opening guitar hook that immediately draws the listener in. They also lauded Langley’s performance and the overall authentic, relatable vibe of the story. As Laura Veltz says, “Songwriters dream of writing songs that can hit all those cylinders at once.”

Below, Veltz, Ashley Gorley , Luke Laird and several other hit songwriters share what they find so enticing about “Choosin’ Texas.” For other records that Langley has set, read more here .
